faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Is it really free to create an online store for my local business?
faq.a1: Yes. The free plan lets any local business list up to 50 products, share its store link and receive orders on WhatsApp with zero commission. A paid plan is available for 50+ products and your own domain.
faq.q2: How do customers order from my shop?
faq.a2: Customers open your store link, add products to the cart and tap "Place Order via WhatsApp". You receive the full itemised bill with delivery address on your WhatsApp.
faq.q3: Do I need a website, app or technical knowledge?
faq.a3: No. Register with your store name and email, add products from your phone or upload an Excel/CSV sheet, and share the link.
faq.a4: Kirana and grocery stores, bakeries, pharmacies, dairy, fruits and vegetables, sweet shops, stationery, hardware and any local shop that delivers or offers pickup.
faq.q5: Do you charge commission on orders?
faq.a5: No. You keep 100% of every order. Customers pay you directly by cash or UPI on delivery.
faq.a6: Once your store has loaded, customers can browse and place orders for 30 minutes even without internet; orders sync automatically when they reconnect.
faq.q7: Do customers need to create an account?
faq.a7: No. Customers can order as guests. An optional account saves their address and shows their order history.
faq.q8: Can I use my own domain name?
faq.a8: Yes, on the paid plan we set up your store on your own domain with your branding. Contact us on WhatsApp.
faq.a9: A villager from Sonsari in Janjgir-Champa district, Chhattisgarh, a village of under 5,000 people. Quick-commerce apps don't deliver there, but mobile data does reach it, so the village's grocers, pickle and papad makers needed a simple way to take orders on WhatsApp. It's free for every local business in India, with zero commission.

story.title: Born in Sonsari, a village in Chhattisgarh
story.p1: Sonsari is a village of under 5,000 people in Janjgir-Champa district, Chhattisgarh. Quick commerce companies don't deliver here, but mobile data now reaches almost every corner.
story.p2: So a villager built this: a simple WhatsApp-based quick commerce for what people already buy locally, from groceries to home-made pickles and papad.
story.p3: It's free for every local business in India, in every Indian language, with zero commission. No aggregator takes a cut, and the shop keeps its own customers.
